questions.q: Why do we prefer woollen clothes in winter?
questions.a: Wool traps air, a poor conductor, so body heat cannot escape and we feel warm.

questions.q: Name three effects of heat that we observe.
questions.a: Rise in temperature, expansion of substances, and change of state (ice to water).

questions.q: What is the normal temperature of the human body?
questions.a: 37 deg C (about 98.6 deg F), measured with a clinical thermometer.

questions.q: What is a clinical thermometer and its range?
questions.a: A thermometer to measure body temperature, reading 35 deg C to 42 deg C.

questions.q: Why should a clinical thermometer not be washed with hot water?
questions.a: Hot water would heat the mercury beyond its range and burst the thermometer.

questions.q: Which thermometer measures the temperature of boiling water?
questions.a: A laboratory thermometer (-10 deg C to 110 deg C), never a clinical one.
Acid + base react to form salt and water, cancelling each other's effect.

questions.q: Give one daily-life use of neutralisation.
questions.a: Antacids neutralise excess stomach acid; lime neutralises acidic soil.

questions.q: What happens to litmus when an acid exactly neutralises a base?
questions.a: The solution turns neutral - red litmus stays red and blue stays blue (no colour change).
